coaching.headline: We won the early scraps, took fuck all from them, then fed Drongo and Sevarog kills for the rest of the night.
coaching.team: We won two early fights and turned neither into a structure, then lost nine structures while taking four. Sevarog got fat off our offlane, the one Fangtooth we took was followed by two of our towers falling, and the third Fangtooth went to them with nobody on our side dead. We placed more wards than they did, but they cleared ten of ours and we cleared one. That is a team that let a free Fangtooth go and left their vision standing.
coaching.lossReflection: The cleanest alternative was early. Those two won fights were the only ones we won all game, and both ended with enemies respawning and nothing taken. Pushing the nearest wave into their outer tower, or setting up the next objective together while they were down, gives a lead something solid to stand on. It would not guarantee the rest of the game, but it beats letting the lead evaporate.

focus.title: Someone dead, nobody fights
focus.action: When one of us is dead, the other four stop picking fights and hold the wave at our nearest tower until the respawn. Whoever sees the death calls it, and nobody plays hero with a tower on the line.

34.1.call: Feng Mao was already dead and the enemy Orb Prime was taken, and the exchange went 2-3 while our inhibitor and Core fell. That was the last fight of the game.

27.3.call: Iggy & Scorch opened by killing Yurei and the exchange still went 2-3, with Drongo finishing Ikra and Feng Mao. Their inner tower and ours both fell in that window. After an opening pick, take the structure and leave before Drongo gets a clean shooting line.

18.1.call: We took their outer tower while their Mini Prime went to them in the same window, and the exchange went 2-3 with Iggy & Scorch and Grux falling first. Before the spawn, the team calls one target, Mini Prime or the tower, and commits to it together.

matchup: Sevarog was the lane opponent; Grux took the first kill, then Sevarog won the later meetings.
Across the match the bigger physical threats were Skylar, their top damage dealer, plus Drongo and Yurei.
build: Sky Splitter, Tainted Rounds and Augmentation all pay through basic attacks, rewarding long contact with one target.
Mistmeadow Buckler's magical armor fits Sevarog, but nothing in the inventory adds physical armor.
eternal: Thraex, Savage Strikes and Ferocity all reward staying on one target.
Golden Mane is a draft alternative to Ferocity if surviving the first exchange is the problem.
augment: Lust For Blood needs a full stack of bleeds first, so it pays in long fights, not against a quick burst.
Red Mist instead grants attack speed per nearby bleeding enemy; neither changes how the first seconds of a fight go.
crest: Iceskorn Talons is a group-fight tool that helps the team stick to a target, not a personal escape.
improvement: Physical armor is the clearest adjustment: Skylar, Drongo and Yurei accounted for half of Grux's deaths.
Tainted Rounds is not the slot to cut; it was the team's earliest anti-heal item against Yurei's and Sevarog's healing.
If armor goes in, it replaces a later damage item such as Augmentation, trading some on-hit damage and haste for survival.

matchup: Belica's Seismic Assault stun and Neural Disruptor silence punish a target standing still, and Drongo's Gag Grenade silences too.
Yurei was the dive threat, resetting on and pulling Soul Ripped targets, and took first blood on Muriel.
build: Marshal's attack speed and on-hit damage suit Ikra's basic-attack build.
Crystal Tear and Transference reward shielding, so the set pays when Muriel shields often.
eternal: Knell, Frequency and Peal are a shred setup on a shield support.
Exarch is the support-oriented draft alternative, trading personal shred for ally damage.
augment: Sacrosanct turns Reversal Of Fortune, the global save, into a fight starter.
Aerial Assistance is the draft alternative if crowd control on the carry is the threat, trading the zone for the escape.
crest: Silentium's extra ward capacity suits a support who placed the most wards in the match.
The silence is a tool for when Belica or Yurei commits.
improvement: If Ikra keeps getting dived, Aerial Assistance on Reversal is the most direct change.
Windcaller gives Muriel and shielded allies movement speed, lighter than Hexbound Bracers' durability; try it only if speed, not survival, is lacking.

matchup: Drongo's bleed and armor shred pressure from range, and Belica's stun and silence punish a carry standing still.
build: Scattershot, Terminus, Viper and Prophecy make this a basic-attack Ikra.
It is consistent, but only Prophecy and the Typhoon crest add magical power, so Brine, Narcosis, Hydroclasm and Genesis get little extra.
eternal: Satariel, Risen and Psychosis are a snowball glass-cannon setup on Ikra, and death removes the Fearless stacks.
Rite is the alternative to Psychosis, trading the target restriction for haste paid in health.
augment: Cascade suits weaving abilities between basic attacks, which is what this build asks for.
The Gloom is the draft alternative if the duo needs protection more than damage.
crest: Typhoon supports the attack-speed plan and adds a small repositioning option against Yurei.
improvement: The low damage is not proven to be the build.
A fair comparison is an ability-power path around Hydroclasm and Brine, trading on-hit consistency for burst.
The field's ability core has weak results, so treat it as an experiment.

matchup: Skylar, their top damage dealer, killed Iggy & Scorch in both opening skirmishes.
Later threats were Yurei and Sevarog, who both reach a mage with no dash beyond Blink, plus Belica's silence.
build: It is a coherent zone-damage build and produced our highest hero damage.
Dreambinder slows, Oblivion Crown multiplies magical power and Tainted Scepter adds anti-heal on magical damage.
eternal: Vesh, Mind Rot and The Tenth Seal fit a hero who keeps enemies standing in fire.
Tithe of Death is the alternative to The Tenth Seal if Inferno is not the main damage source.
augment: Hold This! permanently grows Molotov's damage per hero hit, rewarding landing Molotov from the start.
Turret Maniac trades that ramping damage for a fourth turret, with every turret losing some health.
crest: Epoch's stasis buys time for help against Yurei or Sevarog but gives no distance.
improvement: If Skylar keeps killing Iggy & Scorch early, an early defense against physical damage trades some slow and health for survival.
Tainted Scepter is a choice, not a must: Muriel's passive and Grux's Tainted Rounds also cover Yurei's healing.

matchup: Feng Mao won the head-to-head kills against Yurei, a melee diver who heals and pulls.
Feng Mao's kills mostly landed on Belica and Drongo, the best returns of the match.
build: Manta Scythe, Omen and The Perforator are the field core.
Draconum adds physical armor, healing amplification and a takedown heal, fitting a diver taking repeated physical damage.
eternal: Knell, Frequency and Peal line the follow-up, including an Earth Shatter recast, up against shredded armor.
Fracture is the draft alternative to Peal for longer duels, giving up ultimate haste.
augment: Ichorous Glaive rewards the reset style behind eleven kills but only heals after the kill, not while Drongo is still shooting.
Imperial Duelist is the steadier alternative, trading kill healing for more damage and less damage taken against the current target.
crest: Ortus grants speed and power, and takedowns in the window permanently add power and refresh it, suiting a jungler chasing resets.
improvement: No item swap is proven; dying right after a kill is a decision, not an inventory problem.
If Drongo keeps finishing Feng Mao, a second armor item over a damage slot trades kill pressure for survival.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Support job done where it counts: a hand in 65% of our kills, the most wards on the map, and Ikra never died before the ten-minute mark. That is the standard.

Muriel died first in two early skirmishes: first blood to Yurei, then to Drongo deep in their jungle beside Feng Mao. Before following an early invade, Muriel waits until Yurei is visible; dead supports shield nobody.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Lowest hero damage of our four damage dealers, so Ikra's output is the gap to close. Only three deaths is a decent base; now Willy Guggenheim needs the damage to come with it.

Yurei is the enemy backline diver. When Yurei drops off the map, Willy Guggenheim holds Narcosis for the Severance dash instead of spending Narcosis on poke; the suspend lets Muriel and Grux turn on the diver.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Eleven kills and our highest objective damage. Xeebs was the one actually stabbing people, mostly Belica and Drongo, and that target choice is right.

Three times Feng Mao landed a kill and died seconds later, twice to Drongo. Finishing and then sticking around for the cuddle gets a jungler fucked. After the kill, find Drongo; if Drongo is alive and shooting, leave.
Feng Mao cleared no enemy wards again while they cleared ten of ours. Next game Xeebs calls the Fangtooth plan before each spawn and checks the pit entrances for their vision before the team commits.
b501e4a5-5bdb-4389-9537-8d3b724de144: Grux died to Sevarog five times, and every kill Sevarog lands with an ability adds Souls. After the second loss to Sevarog, hold the wave under tower and call Xeebs before trading again. Good damage, wasted by dying.

Mistmeadow Buckler handles Sevarog's magic, but Skylar, Drongo and Yurei took the other five and nothing in the build stops physical damage. Against three physical threats, physical armor goes in by the third item.
2dfd786d-99cd-4518-8fc0-4fd9de2370c5: Top hero damage on the team, so the output was there. Skylar still killed Iggy & Scorch in both opening skirmishes, so Iggy & Scorch sets turrets and oil before following an invade into Skylar.
The last two deaths went to Yurei. Epoch is built for that exact moment: when Yurei or Sevarog commits onto Iggy & Scorch, stasis buys the team time to turn on the diver.

Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

loadout.plain: Your ultimate comes back faster, and after you land with Reversal of Fortune your hits apply full armor shred at once, so the fight you dive into turns quickly.

lines: Lead story: Soaked the fights. 718 damage mitigated a minute, more than 87% of Muriel support players this patch.
Reversal Of Fortune at rank 3: 135s base, about 87.1s by the end (35% shorter) from 55 ability haste: Marshal 15, Crystal Tear 10, Hexbound Bracers 15, ultimate haste 15.
Muriel dealt 11,313 hero damage, 10% of their team's, with +85 magical power from items.
Hexbound Bracers (item): Restore Mana equal to 15% of damage taken. Reduced to 5% when damaged by Non-Heroes. Based on your Missing Mana, gain 1-3 additional Mana Regen.
Silentium (crest): Silence a Hero for 0.75s. Deals 50 (+20%)(+20%) Damage.

Sustain: 28% heal and shield power; Transference: Upon Shields expiring: 50% of its remaining value is restored as Health over 3s. Reduced to 25% for Ally Shields.; Crystal Tear: On Healing or Shielding Heroes: You both gain 30 Magical Power for 5s. You both gain 15 Ability Haste for 5s.; 11,121 healing recorded.
Toughness: +675 health, +40 physical armor, +40 magical armor; took 23,219 damage, mitigated 25,113, died 3 times.

Loadout augment Sacrosanct: Flying in with Reversal of Fortune drops a Consecrated Ground at the ally you save, healing them and boosting their attack speed while enemies inside attack slower and take magic damage. (game text: Casting Reversal of Fortune on an Allied Hero immediately creates a Consecrated Ground at the current level at the target location.) (changes Consecrated Ground, 14.3s cooldown with their haste) Field: 51% in 2439 games, 41% of picks, below the hero-role's 52%.

Loadout Eternal Knell: Your hits strip the enemy's armor and give some of it to you. Serenity and Consecrated Ground hit several enemies, so your whole team deals more damage to them. (game text: Attacks and abilities against Enemy Heroes apply a stack of Rust for 5s. Each stack shreds 2% (+0.2% per Level) Physical Armor and Magical Armor, stacking up to 4 times. Gain 75% of the Armors shredded.) Field: 51.9% in 231 games, 4% of picks, level the hero-role's 52%.

Loadout minor Frequency: Each armor-shred stack you keep on enemies gives you attack speed and shorter ability cooldowns. Keep landing Serenity and basic attacks to keep the stacks up. (game text: Gain 2% Total Attack Speed and 2 Ability Haste per Rust stack currently applied.)

Loadout minor Peal: Your ultimate comes back faster, and after you land with Reversal of Fortune your hits apply full armor shred at once, so the fight you dive into turns quickly. (game text: Gain 15 Ultimate Ability Haste. Upon casting your ultimate, attacks and abilities apply maximum stacks of Rust for 4s. 20s cooldown.) Field: 53.3% in 150 games, 65% of picks, above the hero-role's 52%.

Loadout crest Silentium: Silence one hero briefly so they cannot cast. Use it on the diver jumping your carry, or to stop an escape before charging a full Serenity stun. Also gives an extra ward. (game text: Muzzle:  Silence a Hero for 0.75s. Deals 50 (+20%)(+20%) Damage. Visionary:  Gain Solstone. Increase Ward Cap from 2 to 3. Pacifist:  Receive diminishing Gold from Minion kills.) Field: 52.2% in 364 games, 6% of picks, level the hero-role's 52%.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 2 effects on one trigger: Marshal, Hexbound Bracers.
Countered? 0 of the 2 players Muriel killed built magical armor. We killed Muriel 3 times.
Copy it? Knell: 51.9% in 231 Muriel support games, level with the hero's 52%. A standard setup: what made it work was this game, not a secret build.
